subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• French chemist Antoine Lavoisier identified oxygen as a distinct element in his 1778 publication Traité Élémentaire de Chimie.
• Lavoisier earned a reputation for being the first person to have discovered oxygen.
• In 2005, historians studying ancient Chinese texts discovered a detailed description of oxygen-producing experiments in a manuscript dating to the 8th century.
• Chinese alchemist Mao Hua had conducted these experiments during the Tang Dynasty, beginning around 750 CE.
• According to chemistry historian Dr. Oksana Kravchenko, these texts suggest that Mao Hua may have isolated oxygen more than a thousand years before Lavoisier's work.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the 2005 discovery to Lavoisier's reputation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Evidence that Mao Hua may have isolated oxygen as early as 750 CE suggests that Lavoisier may not have been the first person to have discovered oxygen.
choices.B: Kravchenko challenged Lavoisier's reputation for being the first person to have discovered oxygen through combustion experiments specifically.
choices.C: According to Kravchenko's analysis of the 2005 discovery, a Chinese alchemist may have conducted oxygen-producing experiments during the Tang Dynasty as early as 750 CE.
choices.D: In 2005, more than two centuries after Lavoisier claimed in his publication that he had identified oxygen, historians uncovered evidence in ancient Chinese texts that disproved his claims.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. Noting that the evidence suggests Mao Hua may have isolated oxygen in 750 CE, the sentence emphasizes how the 2005 discovery challenged Lavoisier's reputation as the first person to discover oxygen.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. While the sentence does emphasize that the discovery challenged Lavoisier's reputation, it misrepresents information in the notes. The notes don't indicate that the 2005 discovery cast any doubt on Lavoisier's claims to have identified oxygen; rather, the discovery challenged Lavoisier's reputation for being the first to discover oxygen.
